safety_data.cardiac_safety_interpretation: In vitro and in vivo safety pharmacology studies indicated that treatment with belinostat is not associated with a significant cardiovascular safety risk, including QTc prolongation.
safety_data.hepatotoxicity_warning: Belinostat can cause fatal hepatotoxicity and liver function test abnormalities. Monitor liver function tests before treatment and before the start of each cycle. Interrupt or adjust dosage until recovery, or permanently discontinue belinostat based on the severity of the hepatic toxicity.
safety_data.lft_monitoring_requirements: Monitor liver function tests before treatment and before the start of each cycle.
safety_data.key_findings: Belinostat administration was not associated with cardiovascular safety risks, including QTc prolongation, based on in vitro and in vivo studies. Toxicity was observed in other systems such as gastrointestinal, genitourinary, hematopoietic, immune, and dermal systems.

treatment_management.toxicity_stopping_criteria: Belinostat was permanently discontinued in patients with recurrent platelet count nadirs of <25×10⁹/L and/or recurrent ANC nadirs of <0.5×10⁹/L after two dose reductions.
treatment_management.treatment_delay_rules: Belinostat treatment could be delayed to allow recovery from toxicities; toxicities had to improve to grade ≤2 prior to retreatment; ANC ≥1.0×10⁹/L and platelet count ≥50×10⁹/L required to resume treatment.
supportive_care_requirements: Supportive care for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea >7 days
treatment_management.dose_modification_rules: Belinostat dose was decreased by 25% when platelet count nadir was <25×10⁹/L and/or ANC nadir was <0.5×10⁹/L; decreased by 25% at first two occurrences of grade 3/4 non-hematologic adverse reactions (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea >7 days with supportive care).
treatment_management.treatment_discontinuation_rules: Belinostat was permanently discontinued in patients with recurrent platelet count nadirs of <25×10⁹/L and/or recurrent ANC nadirs of <0.5×10⁹/L after two dose reductions.

drug_interactions.clinical_significance: Patients homozygous for UGT1A1*28 allele should have a reduced starting dose of Beleodaq to minimize dose-limiting toxicities.

special_populations.pediatric_use: The safety and efficacy of belinostat in pediatric patients have not been established.
special_populations.geriatric_use: In the single-arm trial, 48% of patients (n=62) were ≥65 years of age and 10% of patients (n=13) were ≥75 years of age. The median age of the trial population was 63 years. Patients ≥65 years of age had a higher response rate to belinostat treatment than patients <65 years of age (36% versus 16%) while no meaningful differences in response rate were observed between patients ≥75 years of age and those <75 years of age. No clinically meaningful differences in serious adverse reactions were observed in patients based on age (<65 years compared with ≥65 years or <75 years of age compared with ≥75 years of age).
special_populations.hepatic_impairment_guidance: Belinostat is metabolized in the liver and hepatic impairment is expected to increase exposure to belinostat. Patients with moderate and severe hepatic impairment (total bilirubin >1.5xULN) were excluded from clinical trials. There is insufficient data to recommend a dose of belinostat in patients with moderate and severe hepatic impairment.
special_populations.lactation_guidance: Women should avoid pregnancy while receiving Beleodaq. If this drug is used during pregnancy, or if the patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, the patient should be apprised of potential hazard to the fetus.

formulation_stability.reconstitution_instructions: Reconstitute with 9 mL Sterile Water for Injection to achieve a concentration of 50 mg belinostat/mL. Dilute with 250 mL 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection before infusion.
